meta.title: Meal Planner
meta.subtitle: User manual: plan the family's meals and shopping
meta.author: Hans Tandt

blocks.text: 1. How to use this manual
This manual shows you how to plan the family's meals with Meal Planner. Each chapter is one task. Follow the numbered steps in order.
Numbers in the pictures match the numbers in the text. Coloured boxes give extra help:

rows: A better way. Helpful, but you can skip it.
Something to know, so nothing surprises you.
A mistake to avoid, and what to do instead.

blocks.text: Is the app not on your phone yet? Start with Appendix A, Set up the app on a new phone. Is the app not online yet? Start with Appendix B, Put the app online with Netlify.
The app at a glance

blocks.caption: Figure 1. The week screen: everything starts here.
blocks.alt: The week screen with the week arrows, a day card, the Quick label, the tabs and the menu button marked.

rows: Go to the previous or the next week.
Tap it to see and change that day's meals. Today has an orange border.
The day is busy. The AI chef suggests fast meals for it.
Switch between Week, Shopping and AI Chef.
Backup, language, family name, PIN and API key.

blocks.text: 2. Quick start: plan tonight's dinner
Purpose: add one meal to today in two minutes.

items: Open Meal Planner on your phone.
Enter your 4-digit PIN.
Tap today's card. It has an orange border and the label Today.
Tap Add next to Dinner (1).
Type the name of the meal (2), for example Chicken curry.
Tap Save meal (4).

blocks.caption: Figure 2. Tap Add, type the meal name, then tap Save meal.
blocks.alt: Left: Tuesday with an Add button beside Dinner. Right: the meal editor with the name field, the photo area and the Save meal button marked.

blocks.text: Success: the meal now shows on today's card in the week screen.

blocks.title: Add a photo
blocks.text: Tap the photo area (3) to take a picture of the dish or choose one. The photo then shows on the day card.
3. Plan your week
Purpose: fill the week, change meals and mark busy days.
Go to another week

items: Tap › to see the next week.
Tap ‹ to go back one week.
Tap This week to return to the current week. The button shows only when you look at another week.

blocks.text: Mark a busy day as quick
On busy days there is little time to cook. Mark those days as quick. The AI chef then suggests meals that are ready in 20 minutes or less.

items: Tap the day's card.
Tap the Quick meal day switch (1). It turns orange.
Tap × or anywhere outside the window to close it.

blocks.caption: Figure 3. One day: switch Quick meal day on, and change, remove or add meals.
blocks.alt: Wednesday with the quick switch on, and the pencil, bin and Add buttons marked.

blocks.text: Success: the day card shows the Quick label and an orange stripe on the left.
Change or remove a meal

rows: The pencil (2), or the meal itself

blocks.title: The bin has no undo
blocks.text: The bin removes the meal and its photo at once. If you tap it by mistake, add the meal again.
4. Let the AI chef plan your week
Purpose: get a full week of meals in one tap.
What you need: an internet connection and an API key in the menu. Appendix A shows how to add the key.

items: Mark the busy days as quick (chapter 3).
Tap the AI Chef tab.
Tap Suggest meals.
Wait while the chef plans. This takes a moment.
Read the suggested plan (1). Scroll down to see all 7 days.
Tap Apply to calendar (2).
If the app asks Replace planned meals?, tap Replace (3) or Cancel (4).

blocks.caption: Figure 4. Check the plan, then apply it. Replace only if you want to lose the meals already planned.
blocks.alt: Left: the suggested plan with one day and the Apply to calendar button marked. Right: the Replace planned meals question with Replace and Cancel marked.

blocks.text: Success: the happy chef appears, and the week screen shows the new meals.

blocks.title: Replace overwrites the whole week
blocks.text: Replace removes every meal and photo already planned in that week. Tap Cancel to keep them.

blocks.title: Not happy with the plan?
blocks.text: Tap Suggest meals again for a new plan. Nothing changes until you tap Apply to calendar.

blocks.title: Meal names follow the app language
blocks.text: The chef writes in the language of the app. Chapter 7 shows how to change it.
5. Use the shopping list
Purpose: keep one list per shop and tick items off in the store.

blocks.caption: Figure 5. One list per shop: add, tick and delete items.
blocks.alt: The Delhaize list with the shop buttons, the add field, a tick box, a bin and the AI list button marked.

rows: Tap Delhaize, Lidl, Aldi, Massen or Other. The number shows the items still to buy.
Tap the box. Tap it again to untick.
Let the AI write the list
Tap AI list. See the steps below.

blocks.text: Let the AI write the list

items: Plan the week first (chapter 3 or 4).
Tap the Shopping tab.
Tap AI list (5).
Wait while the chef writes the list.

blocks.text: Success: new items appear under each shop. Items that are already on a list are not added twice.

blocks.title: Which week?
blocks.text: The AI list uses the week you looked at last in the week screen.

blocks.title: Make the list right after planning
blocks.text: Apply the AI plan, then tap AI list. The whole week's shopping is ready in two taps.
6. Recognise a dish and shop for it
Purpose: find out the name of a dish from a photo, and put its ingredients on the shopping list.

items: Tap the AI Chef tab.
Scroll down to Identify a meal.
Tap the photo area, then take or choose a photo.
Tap Identify this meal (1).
Read the name (2) and the description.
Tap Add ingredients to shopping list (3).

blocks.caption: Figure 6. The chef names the dish; one more tap puts its ingredients on the shopping list.
blocks.alt: The Identify this meal button, the dish name and the Add ingredients to shopping list button marked.

blocks.text: Success: the happy chef shows how many ingredients were added. Each ingredient is on the list of the shop where you usually buy it.

blocks.title: Basics are left out
blocks.text: Salt, pepper, cooking oil and water are not added. Items already on a list are not added twice.

blocks.title: Use it while you add a meal
blocks.text: The meal editor has an Identify with AI button too. It fills in the name and the notes for you.
7. Change language, family name and PIN
Purpose: make the app yours. All settings are in the menu ⋮ at the top right.

blocks.caption: Figure 7. The menu holds the backup, language and family settings.
blocks.alt: The menu with Export, Import, the language buttons and the family name field marked.

blocks.text: Change the language

items: Tap ⋮.
Tap English, Français, Nederlands or Deutsch (3).

blocks.text: The app changes language at once. Each phone keeps its own language.
Change the family name

items: Tap ⋮.
Type the name in the Family field (4).
Tap Save family name.

blocks.text: The name shows on the lock screen, at the top of the app and in reports.
Change the PIN

items: Tap ⋮.
Scroll down to Security.
Type your current PIN.
Type a new 4-digit PIN.
Tap Change PIN.

blocks.title: Write your PIN down
blocks.text: The app cannot show or reset a forgotten PIN. Keep it somewhere safe. Chapter 9 shows what to do if it is lost.
8. Back up your data and move it to another phone
Purpose: keep a copy of your meals, photos and lists, and move them to another phone.

blocks.title: Your data lives on the phone
blocks.text: Meals and lists are saved on each phone, not online. Two phones do not share changes on their own.
Make a backup

items: Tap ⋮.
Tap Export data (backup) (1).
Save the file, for example on Google Drive.

blocks.text: The file name looks like tandt-meal-data-2026-10-04.json. It holds the meals, photos, shopping lists and family name.
Restore a backup or move to another phone

items: Open the app on the phone that should receive the data.
Tap ⋮.
Tap Import data (2).
Choose the backup file.

rows: A day is in the file and on this phone
The day from the file replaces the day on this phone.
A day is only on this phone
A shopping item is in the file and on this phone
Items were ticked on the other phone
Ticks are not copied. Tick them again.

blocks.title: Clearing browser data deletes everything
blocks.text: Clearing Brave's site data erases all meals, photos and lists on this phone. Make a backup first.

blocks.title: Back up every week
blocks.text: Export a backup once a week, for example after the big shopping trip.
9. Fix common problems

rows: Tap ⋮ and paste the API key under AI settings. See Appendix A.
The key is wrong or no longer valid. Paste a new key.
Check Wi-Fi or mobile data, then try again.
Try again later, or with another photo.
Free up space on the phone, then save again.
Check the PIN and type it again.
Clear Brave's site data for the app. This removes the PIN and all data on this phone. Then choose a new PIN and import your backup (chapter 8).
The app looks old after an update
Close the app and open it again. In Brave, pull the page down to reload.

blocks.text: Appendix A. Set up the app on a new phone
Purpose: put Meal Planner on a phone for the first time. Do this once per phone.
What you need: the app's web address and an API key (a secret code that lets the app use the AI).

items: Open Brave or Chrome on the phone.
Go to the app's web address.
Choose a 4-digit PIN (Figure 8).
Enter the same PIN again.
Tap ⋮, choose your language and save your family name.
Paste the API key under AI settings, then tap Save API key.
Open the Brave menu and tap Install app or Add to Home screen.

blocks.caption: Figure 8. On a new phone you choose your own PIN. After that, the app asks for it each time you open it.
blocks.alt: The lock screen asking to choose a 4-digit PIN, with the keypad marked.

blocks.text: Success: the chef icon is on your home screen. The app opens full screen from there.

blocks.title: The API key stays on this phone
blocks.text: Each phone needs the key once. Backups never contain the key.

blocks.title: Keep the API key private
blocks.text: Anyone with the key can use the AI at your cost. Do not send it by chat or e-mail.

blocks.title: Where to get an API key
blocks.text: Create one at console.anthropic.com, under API keys. You need an Anthropic account with credit.
Appendix B. Put the app online with Netlify
Purpose: publish the app on the internet, so every phone can open it. Do this on a computer.
What you need: a free Netlify account (a service that hosts websites) and the folder named app.

blocks.caption: Figure 9. Drag the app folder to Netlify; phones then open the web address.
blocks.alt: Three boxes: the app folder on the PC, Netlify, and the phones, joined by arrows labelled drag and address.

blocks.title: Who does this?
blocks.text: Only the person who manages the app. Family members only need Appendix A.
Publish the app for the first time

items: Sign in at app.netlify.com.
Open the Projects page of your team.
Drag the app folder onto the drop area at the bottom of the page.
Wait until the deploy is finished.
Copy the web address that Netlify shows. It ends in .netlify.app.

blocks.text: Success: the web address opens the lock screen in a browser. Now set up each phone with Appendix A.

blocks.title: Sign in before you drop the folder
blocks.text: A folder dropped without signing in stays online for about one hour only. Sign in first, so the app stays online.
Publish an update

items: Sign in at app.netlify.com.
Open your project.
Open the Deploys page.
Drag the whole app folder onto the drop area at the bottom of the page.
Wait until the new deploy is finished.
On the phone, close the app and open it again.

blocks.text: Success: the web address stays the same. Meals, photos and settings stay on each phone.

blocks.title: Drag the folder, not the files inside it
blocks.text: The app folder holds the page, the pictures and the icons together. Without them, the chef pictures and the app icon are missing.
Glossary

rows: The part of the app that suggests meals and recognises dishes.
A secret code that lets the app use the AI chef.
A file with all your meals, photos and lists.
The box for one day in the week screen.
Putting a new version of the app online.
Save a backup file / load a backup file.
The service that keeps the app online at one web address.
The 4-digit code you choose to open the app.
A busy day that gets fast meals.
